examples.knowledge_point: Determining the Area of a Triangle Given a Trigonometric Ratio of an Angle and the Length of a Leg
examples.problem:
Given that $\sin \theta = \dfrac 13,$ calculate the area (in square units) of $\triangle ABC$ shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13946119/assets/3acaffefa93ecbf278a6126661fb9b128ed4f904a22306acd32289eef46d2e0a.png)
examples.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
\mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 AC \cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\sin \theta = \dfrac13,$ where $\theta = m\angle{A}.$ Notice we're also given the length of the side $\overline{BC}$ opposite to $\angle{A}.$ Hence, we can use the sine ratio to find the length of the hypotenuse $\overline{AB}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\frac{BC}{AB} \\ \frac{1}{3} & =\frac{5}{AB} \\ AB & =5(3) \\ AB & =15\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the Pythagorean theorem to find the missing side $AC\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =\sqrt{A{B}^{2}-B{C}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{15}^{2}-{5}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{225-25} \\  & =\sqrt{200} \\  & =10\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 10\sqrt{2}\cdot 5 \\  & =25\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13946119/assets/51e60c645aa6be034a8ef23d16a9ca7a815ca15fe815d7c3b03a866e693f3e5b.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{2}{3},$ the **exact** area of $△ABC$ shown above is{{field-1}} square units.
feedback.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=\frac{2}{3}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AC} \\ \frac{2}{3} & =\frac{10x-1}{8x+2} \\ 2(8x+2) & =3(10x-1) \\ 16x+4 & =30x-3 \\ 14x & =7 \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =10x-1=10(\frac{1}{2})-1=4, \\ AC & =8x+2=8(\frac{1}{2})+2=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 6 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$
